current_hypothesis: The existing Qwen3.5 visual encode should be tested as the first deep visual representation for Frank MVC/open-set routing before adding a second heavy visual backbone; same-request merged feature reuse is physically available through libmtmd but persistent prototype reuse requires an explicit compatibility/lifetime contract.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Raw Qwen/mmproj features may be poorly calibrated for user-specific open-set familiarity, or target runtime/resource behavior may make a dedicated lightweight encoder Pareto-superior.

new_primary_runtime_finding.finding: Current libmtmd stores encoded media output in context/batch-owned std::vector<float> buffers and returns borrowed pointers into those buffers. This supports a same-request feature tap but does not itself define a durable or restart-safe Frank feature handle. Serialized input chunks preserve chunk/preprocessing metadata rather than durable encoded embedding state; loaded placeholder media cannot simply be re-encoded without original media backing.
